questions.q: Explain the mechanism of the Indian monsoon.

answer.text: The monsoon is driven by the different rates at which land and sea heat and cool. In summer the landmass of India and Central Asia heats up strongly, creating a low-pressure area, while the surrounding oceans remain relatively cool with higher pressure.

This pressure difference, together with the northward shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone, draws moist south-west winds from the sea onto the land. Arriving as the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal branches, they bring the heavy rains of June to September, an event called the burst of the monsoon.

In winter the land cools faster than the sea, pressure conditions reverse, and dry north-east winds blow out from the land. These pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and bring rain to the Tamil Nadu coast.
Jet streams, the heating of the Tibetan Plateau, and the El Nino also affect the monsoon's strength.

answer: Thus seasonal reversal of winds governs India's climate.

questions.q: Why does India receive most of its rainfall in the summer, and how does the monsoon affect life?

answer.text: receives most of its rain in summer because of the southwest monsoon, driven by the heating of the land.

list: In summer the land heats up and forms a low-pressure area that draws in moist winds from the sea
These southwest winds bring heavy rain from June to September
Farming, and hence food and the rural economy, revolve around the timely arrival of the rains
A good monsoon brings prosperity; a weak or late one brings drought and hardship, so the whole nation awaits it

questions.q: Why is rainfall in India so variable, and what problems does this create?

answer.text: is very uneven in space and time, because it depends on the changeable monsoon and on relief.

list: Some regions like the Western Ghats and the northeast get very heavy rain, while others like western Rajasthan get very little
The monsoon can arrive early or late and give more or less rain from year to year

answer.text: It brings both floods and droughts.

list: Areas of heavy rain may suffer floods, while areas of scanty or failed rain face drought and crop failure
This makes water management, irrigation and drought relief essential across India
